{{Short description|On when a 3-manifold is homeomorphic to the 3-sphere}}
In [[topology]], a branch of [[mathematics]], '''Bing's recognition theorem''', named for [[R. H. Bing]], asserts that a necessary and sufficient condition for a {{nowrap|[[3-manifold]]}} ''M'' to be [[homeomorphic]] to the {{nowrap|[[3-sphere]]}} is that every [[Jordan curve]] in ''M'' be contained within a topological [[ball (mathematics)|ball]]. It is a weak version of the [[Poincaré conjecture]].
